messages:
Incident Bot: [ALERT] p99 latency breach for tenant=novahealth in eu-west-2 dedicated pool 'dedicated-eu-west-2-nova' — p95=2.1s (baseline 140ms), p99=7.8s, error_rate=0.42% — triggered at 2028-02-03T16:07:14Z
Derek (oncall): I'm paged, coming in. Looks like dedicated pool saturation? I'll join war room.
Tilly (SRE): I can see the same in metrics. CPU/GPU utilization on pool nodes is pegged, queue depth spiking. No global outage, scope is novahealth's pool in eu-west-2.
Carol (ML Eng): checked model backend for novahealth — KV cache size exploded after a gradual traffic increase; reuse rate low. Might be cache churn causing heavy host memory->disk pressure on the inference hosts.
Ben (Infra): Confirmed. Disk io is high on two nodes (node ids: i-0a2b3c4d, i-0f9e8d7c). Autoscale didn't kick because pool is at reserve limit (customer reserved capacity).
Alice (Support): NovaHealth ops on call pinged us: "We're seeing slow responses in our production workflows, P99s ~8s, impacting claim processing." They've requested ETA and mitigation steps.
Derek (oncall): Priority: restore acceptable latency for customer ASAP. Options: 1) Warm failover to eu-central standby (we have cold warm replicas), 2) Route a % traffic to hosted fallback with model variant, 3) Increase capacity on dedicated pool (requires manual approval for reserved pool), 4) Per-tenant throttling/rate-limit to shed load.
Tilly (SRE): Immediate safe action: enable routing of a controlled percentage to eu-central and enable per-tenant throttling at 90% of current baseline to reduce burst. I'll run routing changes now.
Carol (ML Eng): Also propose enabling the smaller model variant for novahealth as temporary fallback: model=fallback-small-quant. This will reduce latency and memory. I'll prepare the model rollout.
Ben (Infra): Scaling note: since it's a reserved pool we can bump capacity via infra action but it needs approval from infra leads; I can start warm nodes to avoid slow cold boots, but they won't register until we toggle pool quota.
Derek (oncall): Tilly, please apply the routing. Carol, prepare the model fallback. Ben, start warm nodes in parallel. Alice, keep NovaHealth updated with an ETA.
Tilly (SRE): Running route change: (command)
```
# route 30% of novahealth traffic from dedicated-eu-west-2-nova -> dedicated-eu-central-standby
rwctl routing create --tenant novahealth --from-pool dedicated-eu-west-2-nova --to-pool dedicated-eu-central-standby --percent 30 --sticky false
```
Tilly (SRE): Route change applied. Monitoring ingress in eu-central.
Carol (ML Eng): Preparing fallback model rollout: will deploy serving variant 'rwd-fallback-small-q4' to eu-central and eu-west-2 standby. Config snippet:
```
model_rollout {
  tenant: novahealth
  from: rwd-production-1
  to: rwd-fallback-small-q4
  traffic_split: 30
}
```
Carol (ML Eng): Triggered rollout via deploy job.
Ben (Infra): Started two warm nodes in eu-central pool. Node bootstrap logs show healthy; attaching to pool in 90s.
Derek (oncall): Observability: p95/p99 in eu-west-2 after route change?
Tilly (SRE): After 5m: eu-west-2 p95 down to 380ms, p99 down to 1.6s. Overall p99 for tenant across regions ~1.9s. Error rate normalized to 0.05%. Trending improving.
Alice (Support): Updated NovaHealth: "We've routed ~30% of traffic to EU-CENTRAL standby and applied rate-limiting to non-critical paths. Expecting latency improvements within 10m. We'll keep you posted." They replied: ":+1: thank you, please continue"
Eve (Prod Eng): Any correlation with recent deploys? I see a quantization change on rwd-production-1 pushed 2 hours ago for novahealth. Carol, could that be related?
Carol (ML Eng): Good catch — the quantized build had a bug that increases KV churn under certain sequence patterns. I'm rolling back the quantized change for novahealth specifically. Rollback command:
```
rwctl model rollback --tenant novahealth --model rwd-production-1 --to-version v1.23
```
Carol (ML Eng): Rollback issued.
Tilly (SRE): 12m after rollback + routing + fallback model partial rollout: p95=160ms, p99=320ms in eu-west-2; overall p99 ~300ms. Looks stable.
Derek (oncall): Good. Now we need a secure mitigations checklist for post-incident: why autoscale didn't kick (reserve limit), add early alarms for KV churn, update reserved pool escalation path, and confirm customer compensation policy if SLA hit.
Ben (Infra): I'll open infra ticket to allow temporary emergency capacity override for reserved pools and document the manual steps we took.
Alice (Support): NovaHealth wants a short incident summary and timeline within 2 hours. I'll draft and send once we have final metrics.
Eve (Prod Eng): Also recommend adding a canary for quantized builds that targets low-traffic tenants before wide rollout. I'll file a PR.
Derek (oncall): Handoff: I'm handing to Ben for overnight monitoring. Ben, you'll be primary?
Ben (Infra): Taking handoff. I'll keep watch and escalate to Tilly/Carol if we get a new spike.
Derek (oncall): Thx team. Quick notes for post-incident: root-cause likely interplay of quantized model causing KV churn + reserved pool saturation + no emergency override. Action owners: Carol (model rollback + canary), Ben (infra emergency override + ticket), Tilly (alarms and routing playbook), Alice (customer comms).
Tilly (SRE): Creating incident channel and postmortem ticket: INC-2028-042-novahealth-latency. I'll include grafana snapshots and the command history.
Alice (Support): Drafted initial update for NovaHealth and sent. They acknowledged and asked for a timezone-friendly follow-up tomorrow morning.
Ben (Infra): Monitoring check: all nodes healthy, no new disk pressure. I'll leave autoscaling probes active and alert if queue depth > 50 for >5m.
Derek (oncall): Closing war room. If any regressions, ping the incident channel. Great job — quick coordinated response. :handshake:
Tilly (SRE): Adding runbook entry and automating the 30% cross-region routing command as a playbook for similar tenant-level saturation events.
Carol (ML Eng): I'll prepare a short rollback postmortem for the quantized change and start the canary PR.
Alice (Support): I'll attach NovaHealth timeline and the message we sent to the postmortem ticket.
Incident Bot: Incident marked resolved by Derek (oncall) — duration 32m.
